title: What If We Rode Nuclear Bombs to Saturn? The US Had a Plan

scenes.text: What if a spaceship flew by exploding nuclear bombs behind it? America spent seven years building one.
Project Orion, 1958 to 1965. A 4,000-ton ship the height of a twenty-story building, with a thousand-ton steel plate on the bottom.
Every second or so, a small bomb pops out behind the plate and detonates. The blast shoves the ship forward. 2,600 bombs for one mission.
Giant shock absorbers smooth the jolts to about two to four g. The physicists' slogan: Saturn by 1970.
In 1959 they flew a one-meter model on ordinary explosives. It climbed 185 feet and parachuted down intact.
Then the problem: fallout, estimated at about ten deaths per launch. The 1963 Test Ban Treaty ended it. The fastest ship ever designed never flew.

description:
What if we rode nuclear bombs to Saturn? From 1958 to 1965 Project Orion designed a 4,000-ton spaceship propelled by 2,600 small nuclear bombs detonated behind a 1,000-ton pusher plate, with shock absorbers holding the ride to about 2 to 4 g.
A scale model flew on conventional explosives in 1959, but fallout estimates of around ten deaths per launch and the 1963 nuclear test ban treaty killed the project.
